Unit 9 - Precision & Concision — Title & Goal
Learn to master unit 9 - precision & concision questions for the Digital SAT through a short concept, a modeled item, and targeted practice.

Key skill

Read the note and focus on what the question is really asking inside the passage.

  • Use context to define words.
  • Prefer precise, concise wording.
  • Match tone to situation (formal/informal).

Model item

Study how the evidence in the passage supports the correct answer.

Sentence — The instructions were so convoluted that even experts needed a diagram.

Question 1. As used in the sentence, “convoluted” most nearly means

  • complex
  • polite
  • ancient
  • predictable
Context indicates complexity → A.

Quick practice

Try these quickly. Eliminate two choices before choosing your answer.

Sentence — The memo asks for a response at your earliest convenience.

Question 2. Which choice best maintains a formal tone?

  • ASAP
  • right away
  • convenience
  • whenever

Next skill

Build on the previous skill. Compare how this question type reads the passage differently.

Note: Locate the exact phrase or sentence that proves your choice.

Another model item

Notice how small wording differences change the best answer.

Sentence — The report is very extremely detailed.

Question 3. Which revision is most concise and appropriate?

  • very detailed
  • extremely detailed
  • detailed
  • detailed in nature

More practice

Aim for accuracy first, then speed. Re-check the evidence that rules out each wrong choice.

Sentence — The team reached a mutual consensus.

Question 4. Which choice avoids redundancy?

  • mutual consensus
  • consensus
  • shared consensus
  • mutual agreement consensus

Mixed practice set

These mix multiple skills. Mark the question type before you start, then solve.

Sentence — The CEO spoke in a candid tone about challenges.

Question 5. Which choice best preserves the meaning of “candid”?

  • frank
  • ornate
  • hesitant
  • secretive
